newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatists bomb empty holiday villas.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatists bomb empty holiday villas.

text.p: Corsican separatists bombed and destroyed four empty villas on a holiday estate on the French Mediterranean island overnight, police said on Monday.
About 20 hooded gunmen raided the estate after seizing the keeper. Police said they defused one bomb after the attack.

There were no casualties in the attack which was claimed by the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), a new group using the name of the island's first separatist movement. The original group has split into the FLNC-Historic wing and FLNC-Usual wing.
The attack was seen as a response to the government crackdown on A Cuncolta Naziunalista, the political arm of the FLNC-Historic wing.
Three leaders of the group have been detained in the past week and remanded in custody in Paris for suspected membership of a terrorist group and offences against weapons laws.

The FLNC first surfaced last May when its hooded leaders held a clandestine news conference near Ajaccio and announced they would use violence if the interests of the Corsican people were being threatened.

French police launched a crackdown on Corsican separatists after FLNC-Historic wing guerrillas bombed the Bordeaux mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe last month and staged other bomb attacks on the French mainland.
